Subject: Advance invoice payment — currency & bank routing question

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the invoice. We're ready to initiate the advance payment for INV-2027-349 but have a couple of constraints from our treasury team: they want to pay in EUR from our Frankfurt account and avoid unexpected correspondent bank charges eating into the advance amount. Two quick questions:

1) Can Redwood receive the EUR payment into a Euro-denominated account (IBAN) so that our bank will not have to route through USD rails?
2) If an intermediary bank is used by our payment path, do you invoice net (i.e., we pay gross and Redwood absorbs intermediary fees) or do you expect Brightline to top-up to cover correspondent/clearing fees? Also, any advice on VAT handling — we're buying a pre-paid credit package. We can provide our German VAT ID if that changes treatment.

I'm attaching our wire form (filled). Happy to hop on a short call if easier.

Best,
Daniel

From: soojin.lee@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Advance invoice payment — currency & bank routing question

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear note and for attaching the wire form. Quick answers and recommended routing below.

Summary answers:
- Yes, we can accept EUR into our Euro account (preferred) so your Frankfurt treasury can send a SEPA/EUR wire and avoid USD rails.
- By default our invoices are gross amounts (Brightline pays the invoiced EUR). If correspondent/intermediary fees occur and reduce the net received amount, we typically ask customers to cover the shortfall.

Proposal for this payment (to avoid surprises):
1) Preferred: SEPA / EUR credit to our Euro account — no correspondent. Details:
   - Bank: Deutsche Bank AG
   - Beneficiary: Redwood Inference Ltd. (Euro Account)
   - IBAN: DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00
   - BIC/SWIFT: DEUTDEFFXXX
   - Reference/Memo: INV-2027-349 / Brightline Health GmbH

2) If your bank routes through an intermediary and the payment arrives net of fees, we can either:  (a) ask Brightline to cover the shortfall with a small top-up wire OR (b) accept the net amount and Redwood will issue a corrected credit note for the difference once you provide the MT103 (proof of payment) — we normally prefer (a) for bookkeeping simplicity.

3) VAT note: Since this is a B2B supply of pre-paid credits to a German VAT-registered company, if you provide a valid German VAT ID (USt-IdNr) we can issue an invoice with reverse-charge (VAT not charged) — please attach your VAT ID on the payment reference or send it to laura.bennett@redwood.com. If no VAT ID is provided we will invoice with German VAT as required.

Attachments: billing team has pre-populated an alternate wire template and an internal note about typical correspondent banks (e.g., some banks route via HSBC UK which can introduce a fixed EUR intermediary fee of ~€12–€25).

If you'd like, Ben can monitor the incoming payment and confirm the exact net received so we can reconcile quickly.

Best,
Soogin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: INV-2027-349-advance.pdf (Invoice, 18 KB)]

Hi Daniel / Soojin — adding the finance perspective and payment confirmation steps.

Actionable instructions for Brightline treasury to avoid intermediary fees:
1) SEPA credit to the IBAN above (DEUTDEFFXXX) will not route through USD and should avoid correspondent charges. Please ensure the payment is sent as "OUR" or "SHA with OUR" (i.e., the originator covers any sending-bank fees) so it arrives for the full invoice amount. If your bank insists on using "BEN" or routes through a third-party correspondent, please include a short note in the payment reference so we can match MT103.

2) If an intermediary fee appears and you cannot prevent it, Redwood can offer a one-time partial concession for this pilot:
   - We will credit up to €25 to Brightline within the next billing cycle upon receipt of the MT103 showing the intermediary deduction.
   - For bookkeeping we need: a) exact gross amount sent, b) MT103 trace, and c) date/time of payment.

3) VAT handling: Please send your German VAT ID to me (laura.bennett@redwood.com). Once we validate your VAT ID we will re-issue the invoice with reverse-charge text and zero VAT.

Ben will watch for the incoming payment and confirm within 24 hours of receipt. If you prefer a local EUR collection arrangement (local entity / marketplace payout) we can explore for future settlements but for now SEPA to the IBAN above is fastest.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
